title: The console look
summary: The game takes the look of the map-console reference. The GUI is dark teal glass with glowing cyan borders and orange for whatever is active, the same everywhere instead of changing with each empire's space. Rajdhani headings, a planet card at the bottom right in space, and a planet map like the console's terrain map: glowing coasts, orange routes, circled icons, a compass, a scale bar and toggleable layers. The system and galaxy maps use the same circled glyphs, and the tabs have icons that say what they are. Every ship leaves a billowing, crackling exhaust trail after the 80s-anime jets reference, and the ship, station and character sprites got an 80s-anime cel-shaded look with ink outlines, their designs unchanged. The scanner's signal paths and animations became glowing routes, rings and sweeps, and trail plumes far out in signal sites no longer fail to draw.

steps.title: One look, after the console reference
steps.text: The whole GUI follows the map-console reference now, and it no longer changes colour with the empire whose space you're in. The panels are dark teal glass with thin glowing cyan borders. Orange marks whatever is active: the selected tab is lit orange, buttons glow orange on hover, and every panel has orange trims on its cut corners. Headings, tabs and big buttons use Rajdhani, a squared techno font. Every panel built in code gets the same frame, whatever colour it used to ask for.

steps.title: The planet card
steps.text: The reference's sector panel became a planet card at the bottom right in space. It shows the planet under the mouse, or the one you're close to: its name and kind, a picture of it seen from orbit and lit by its star, its system, orbit, moons, whether you can land and the local threat, then its description. It fades in and out, and the planet map uses it too, with the surface's facts.

steps.title: Exhaust trails for every ship
steps.text: Every ship leaves an exhaust trail in the style of the reference sheet. It's billowing smoke in flat cel-shaded tones that darkens as it drifts back, with crackling lightning streaks inside and a white-hot plume at the nozzle. Trails follow where the nozzle has been, so turns leave curves, and each puff fades after 1.6 seconds. A trail is at most five ship lengths long, about a quarter of the window for yours. You and the Athenians and Ionians burn blue; pirates, Spartans and hostiles burn orange; the others burn magenta. Frame rate is unchanged.

diagram.text: cel-shaded puffs  ·  lightning streaks  ·  a white-hot plume  ·  1.6 s life  ·  up to 5 ship lengths

steps.title: The planet map, like the console's
steps.text: The planet map is drawn after the reference's terrain map. The sea is deep navy with a faint grid, the land dark teal tinted by its terrain and hillshaded from its broad slopes, with the ridges facing the light lit orange, and the coastlines glow cyan. Orange routes run from your ship to every settlement, with dotted cyan ones between them. Settlements are circled icons (a temple for the palace), pirates are red warning badges, and a compass and a scale bar complete it. A LAYERS panel switches routes, places, people and the grid on and off, and the planet's card sits in the corner. Hovering a settlement names it; clicking walks you there.

diagram.text: sea navy with a faint grid  ·  land teal, hillshaded, ridges lit orange  ·  coasts glowing cyan

steps.title: Map icons in the same style
steps.text: The system and galaxy maps use the console's markers: a glowing ring on dark glass with a line glyph inside, cyan for places, orange for you and whatever is active, red for danger. On the system map the star, planets (with ringed and moon variants), stations, gates, signals, survey points and the objective each have their own glyph. Planets keep their small shaded disc inside a ring that turns orange where you can land, ships are arrows pointing the way they fly, and your course is an orange glowing route. On the galaxy map systems are circled stars ringed in their owner's colour, the lanes are dotted cyan (red at war fronts), and a planned route glows orange.

diagram.text: MapIcons: a glowing ring on dark glass with a line glyph - cyan places, orange you and the active, red danger
system map: planets keep their shaded disc inside the ring (orange when you can land); ships are arrows
galaxy map: circled stars ringed in the owner's colour, dotted cyan lanes (red at war), the route glowing orange

steps.title: Icons that say what they are
steps.text: The Ship Computer's tabs got glowing line icons that match their pages: a journal for the quest, a cargo crate for the inventory instead of a shopping cart, a circuit tree for research instead of a star, an open book, an info badge, a planet with its orbit and moon, and a spiral galaxy instead of a crosshair. Every other icon in the game now uses the theme's cyan and orange instead of blue and gold.

diagram.text: glowing line icons; every other icon now in the theme's cyan and orange

steps.title: An 80s-anime look for the sprites
steps.text: Every ship, station and character sprite was restyled toward 80s anime without changing its design. A new tool smooths away fine surface noise, snaps the shading to four flat cel tones, livens the colours and adds a bright rim along the edges facing the light and a bold ink outline. That covers 73 ships, 24 stations, the two citizen portraits and the 240 body parts of the planet characters. Building tiles (they'd show seams) and effects (glows) were left alone. The untouched originals are kept outside the game, so the look can be re-run with other settings or removed.

diagram.text: tools/anime_style.py bakes the look into data/sprites - the designs stay the same
the untouched PNGs are kept in external/sprite_originals/ (re-runs start from them; --restore puts them back)
left alone: building tiles (they'd seam) and effects (glows)

steps.title: Signal paths as glowing routes
steps.text: The paths to located signals now look like the reference's routes. Each one is a gentle curve from your ship to the signal, drawn as a wide soft glow with a bright core in the signal's colour, light nodes along it, pulses of light running out, and glowing rings at the signal. The chevrons are gone. The paths keep the same width at any zoom and still fade away with the scan.

diagram.text: glow, core, nodes, light pulses running out, rings at the signal - no arrows

steps.title: Scanner animations in the same style
steps.text: The scanner's animations match the routes. A system scan sends out rings that each have a soft glow, a bright core and light nodes turning around them, with a radar sweep from an orange hub at your ship. Scanning an asteroid fires a glowing beam with pulses running to the rock. Target rings with turning nodes circle the rock while an orange arc fills as the scan runs, under a SCANNING readout. A scanned rock keeps a glowing ring in its ore's colour. Every part keeps the same size at any zoom.

diagram.text: system scan: glowing rings with nodes, a radar sweep

asteroid scan: a glowing beam with pulses,
target rings with nodes, an orange progress arc

steps.title: Fix: trail plumes far out
steps.text: A test now and then hit "Invalid polygon data, triangulation failed" in a signal site. Sites are played very far out, at 240,000 in each direction, and at coordinates that large a ship's small plume triangle lost precision in the renderer and collapsed. The plume is now drawn around its own nozzle, and two other spots skip shapes too thin to fill.

review.intro: Patch 0006 gives the game the map-console reference's look: one GUI palette (dark teal glass, cyan borders, orange highlights) instead of a palette per empire, Rajdhani headings, a planet card, the planet map redrawn like the console's terrain map, circled map icons for the system and galaxy maps and tab icons that fit their pages. Every ship gets an exhaust trail after the 80s-anime jets reference, and the sprites an 80s-anime cel look (tools/anime_style.py). The scanner's signal paths and animations became glowing routes, rings and sweeps. Plus a precision fix for trail plumes far out in signal sites.

+## nozzle position, heading and thrust each frame (player Ship or Enemy).
+
+const STYLES := {
+	# cloud near the nozzle, cloud far back, streaks / core, plume tip
+	"blue": [Color(0.16, 0.56, 1.0), Color(0.12, 0.3, 0.8), Color(0.72, 0.95, 1.0), Color(0.35, 0.8, 1.0)],
+	"orange": [Color(1.0, 0.5, 0.1), Color(0.8, 0.28, 0.12), Color(1.0, 0.92, 0.55), Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.2)],
+	"magenta": [Color(0.98, 0.28, 0.78), Color(0.56, 0.3, 0.9), Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.96), Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.85)],
+}
+const LIFE := 1.6                   # seconds a puff of exhaust lasts
+const SPACING := 9.0                # px between trail points
+const STREAKS := 3
+
+var ship: Node2D
+var style := "blue"
+var width := 14.0                   # the cloud's half-width at its fullest
+var max_len := 600.0                # never longer than this (px)
+var _pts: Array = []                # [{p: Vector2, t: float born, k: thrust 0..1, s: seed}]
+var _time := 0.0
+var _glow: Node2D                   # additive layer: streaks, core and plume
+var _flick := 0                     # re-jags the streaks a few times a second
+var _seed := 0
+var _count := 0                    # points made so far (puffs follow it)
+
+
+## Gives `ship` a trail (sized from its length): returns it.
+static func attach(s: Node2D, trail_style: String, ship_length: float) -> ExhaustTrail:
+	var t := ExhaustTrail.new()
+	t.ship = s
+	t.style = trail_style if STYLES.has(trail_style) else "blue"
+	t.width = clampf(ship_length * 0.22, 11.0, 50.0)
+	t.max_len = clampf(ship_length * 5.0, 320.0, 760.0)
+	s.add_child(t)
+	return t
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	name = "ExhaustTrail"
+	top_level = true                # (world coordinates: the trail stays where it was left)
+	z_as_relative = true
+	z_index = -1
+	_seed = randi()
+	_glow = Node2D.new()
+	_glow.top_level = true
+	_glow.z_index = -1
+	var m := CanvasItemMaterial.new()
+	m.blend_mode = CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_ADD
+	_glow.material = m
+	_glow.draw.connect(_draw_glow)
+	add_child(_glow)
+
+
+## The ship's nozzle (world), backwards direction and thrust 0..1.
+func _engine() -> Array:
+	if ship.get("engine_offset") != null:   # the player's Ship: rotates as a whole, nose to -Y
+		var back: Vector2 = (ship.global_transform.basis_xform(Vector2(0, 1))).normalized()
+		var nozzle: Vector2 = ship.global_transform * (ship.engine_offset + Vector2(0, 4))
+		var boost := 1.25 if float(ship.get("boost_time")) > 0.0 else 1.0
+		return [nozzle, back, clampf(float(ship.thrust) * boost, 0.0, 1.3)]
+	# An Enemy: its body turns (nose to -Y), the node doesn't.
+	var body: Node2D = ship.get("body")
+	var rot: float = body.global_rotation if body else 0.0
+	var back2 := Vector2(0, 1).rotated(rot)
+	var half: float = float(ship.get("_half_height")) if ship.get("_half_height") != null else 40.0
+	var v: Vector2 = ship.get("velocity") if ship.get("velocity") != null else Vector2.ZERO
+	var top: float = maxf(float(ship.get("max_speed")), 1.0)
+	return [ship.global_position + back2 * half * 0.82, back2, clampf(v.length() / top, 0.0, 1.0)]
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_time += delta
+	global_position = Vector2.ZERO
+	global_rotation = 0.0
+	_glow.global_position = Vector2.ZERO
+	var alive: bool = is_instance_valid(ship) and ship.has_method("is_alive") and ship.is_alive() and ship.visible
+	if alive:
+		var e := _engine()
+		var nozzle: Vector2 = e[0]
+		var k: float = e[2]
+		# The newest point rides the nozzle; once it's SPACING past the last
+		# fixed one it stays put and a new one starts.
+		if _pts.size() < 2 or nozzle.distance_to(_pts[1]["p"]) >= SPACING:
+			_count += 1
+			_pts.push_front({"p": nozzle, "t": _time, "k": k, "s": float(_count)})
+		else:
+			_pts[0]["p"] = nozzle
+			_pts[0]["k"] = k
+			_pts[0]["t"] = _time
+	# Old puffs fade out; the trail never grows past max_len.
+	var total := 0.0
+	var keep := 0
+	for i in _pts.size():
+		if _time - float(_pts[i]["t"]) > LIFE:
+			break
+		if i > 0:
+			total += _pts[i]["p"].distance_to(_pts[i - 1]["p"])
+			if total > max_len:
+				break
+		keep = i + 1
+	_pts.resize(keep)
+	if Engine.get_process_frames() % 4 == 0:
+		_flick += 1
+	queue_redraw()
+	_glow.queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _on_screen() -> bool:
+	if _pts.is_empty():
+		return false
+	var vr := get_viewport_rect()
+	var ct := get_canvas_transform()
+	var p: Vector2 = ct * _pts[0]["p"]
+	return vr.grow(max_len * ct.get_scale().x + 50.0).has_point(p)
+
+
+## Per point: the side vector, distance along the trail (0..1) and fade.
+func _frame() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	var along := 0.0
+	for i in _pts.size():
+		var p: Vector2 = _pts[i]["p"]
+		if i > 0:
+			along += p.distance_to(_pts[i - 1]["p"])
+		var a: Vector2 = _pts[maxi(i - 1, 0)]["p"]
+		var b: Vector2 = _pts[mini(i + 1, _pts.size() - 1)]["p"]
+		var dir := (b - a)
+		if dir.length() < 0.01:
+			dir = Vector2(0, 1)
+		var side := dir.normalized().orthogonal()
+		var age := (_time - float(_pts[i]["t"])) / LIFE
+		var fade := pow(clampf(1.0 - age, 0.0, 1.0), 1.4) * clampf(float(_pts[i]["k"]) * 1.4, 0.0, 1.0)
+		out.append([p, side, along, age, fade])
+	for f in out:
+		f[2] = f[2] / maxf(max_len, 1.0)
+	return out
+
+
+## The cloud's half-width at a point: narrow at the nozzle, billowing out as
+## it spreads with age, lumpy (each puff its own size), tapering to a thin tip.
+func _half(u: float, age: float, seed: float) -> float:
+	var grow := 0.3 + 0.7 * smoothstep(0.0, 0.28, u)
+	var tip := pow(1.0 - smoothstep(0.42, 1.0, u), 1.2)
+	# Puffs: round billows of different sizes, fixed to the exhaust as it drifts.
+	var lump := 0.78 + 0.22 * sin(seed * 0.83) + 0.12 * sin(seed * 2.1 + 1.0)
+	return width * grow * tip * lump * (1.0 + 1.1 * age * (1.0 - u * 0.6))
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	if not _on_screen() or _pts.size() < 2:
+		return
+	var s: Array = STYLES[style]
+	var f := _frame()
+	# The billowing exhaust, cel-shaded like the reference: round puffs in three
+	# flat tones - a darker shade on one side, the body, a light band along the
+	# other - drawn tail first so the fresh puffs sit on top.
+	for tone in 3:
+		for i in range(f.size() - 1, -1, -1):
+			var e: Array = f[i]
+			var a: float = clampf(e[4] * 1.8, 0.0, 1.0)   # (opaque, like the reference, until the tail fades)
+			if a <= 0.02:
+				continue
+			var r := _half(e[2], e[3], _pts[i]["s"])
+			if r < 0.8:
+				continue
+			var col: Color = s[0].lerp(s[1], clampf(e[2] * 1.2, 0.0, 1.0))
+			var side: Vector2 = e[1]
+			match tone:
+				0:
+					_puff(e[0] + side * r * 0.18, r * 1.06, Color(col.darkened(0.42), 0.9 * a))
+				1:
+					_puff(e[0] - side * r * 0.04, r * 0.9, Color(col, 0.92 * a))
+				2:
+					_puff(e[0] - side * r * 0.34, r * 0.46, Color(col.lightened(0.3), 0.8 * a))
+
+
+func _puff(at: Vector2, r: float, c: Color) -> void:
+	draw_circle(at, r, c, true, -1.0, true)
+
+
+func _draw_glow() -> void:
+	if not _on_screen() or _pts.size() < 2:
+		return
+	var s: Array = STYLES[style]
+	var f := _frame()
+	var ci := _glow
+	# The hot core: white-hot near the nozzle, gone a quarter of the way back.
+	var core := PackedVector2Array()
+	var core_c := PackedColorArray()
+	for e in f:
+		if e[2] > 0.28:
+			break
+		core.append(e[0])
+		core_c.append(Color(s[2], e[4] * 0.8 * (1.0 - e[2] / 0.28)))
+	if core.size() >= 2:
+		ci.draw_polyline_colors(core, core_c, width * 0.45, true)
+	# Lightning-like streaks crackling through the cloud (re-jagged often).
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	for k in STREAKS:
+		rng.seed = hash([_seed, k, _flick])
+		var line := PackedVector2Array()
+		var cols := PackedColorArray()
+		var ph := rng.randf() * TAU
+		for i in f.size():
+			var e: Array = f[i]
+			if e[2] > 0.9:
+				break
+			var w := _half(e[2], e[3], _pts[i]["s"]) * 0.7
+			var off := sin(ph + e[2] * (9.0 + k * 4.0) + _time * 3.0) * 0.55 + rng.randf_range(-0.25, 0.25)
+			line.append(e[0] + e[1] * w * off)
+			cols.append(Color(s[2], e[4] * (1.0 - 0.2 * k) * (1.0 - e[2] * 0.8)))
+		if line.size() >= 2:
+			ci.draw_polyline_colors(line, cols, 2.2 if k == 0 else 1.4, true)
+	# The plume: white-hot at the nozzle, a flame of the trail's colour behind.
+	if is_instance_valid(ship) and ship.has_method("is_alive") and ship.is_alive():
+		var e2 := _engine()
+		var k2: float = e2[2]
+		if k2 > 0.03:
+			var at: Vector2 = e2[0]
+			var back: Vector2 = e2[1]
+			var side: Vector2 = back.orthogonal()
+			var length := width * (2.2 + 2.0 * k2) * randf_range(0.9, 1.1)
+			var wd := width * 0.5
+			if not (at.is_finite() and back.is_finite()) or back.length() < 0.5 or length < 2.0:
+				return
+			# (Drawn round the nozzle, not in world coordinates: far out - the signal
+			# sites at 240000 - a small triangle loses precision and fails.)
+			ci.draw_set_transform(at)
+			ci.draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([side * wd, -side * wd, back * length]), Color(s[3], 0.55 * k2))
+			ci.draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([side * wd * 0.5, -side * wd * 0.5, back * length * 0.6]), Color(1, 1, 1, 0.75 * k2))
+			ci.draw_circle(Vector2.ZERO, wd * 1.6, Color(s[3], 0.22 * k2))
+			ci.draw_circle(Vector2.ZERO, wd * 0.75, Color(1, 1, 1, 0.65 * k2))
+			ci.draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO)

@@ -1,0 +1,125 @@ 
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""80s-anime look for the game's sprites (after the exhaust-trail reference sheet's
+jets): bold dark outlines, cel shading in a few flat tones, livelier colours and a
+bright rim along the edges facing the light (top left) - the designs themselves
+stay as they are.
+
+The untouched PNGs are kept in external/sprite_originals/ (copied there the first
+time a sprite is styled); data/sprites/<key>.png is always made from that copy, so
+running this again (or with other settings) never compounds.
+
+  python3 tools/anime_style.py              -> ships, stations, citizens
+  python3 tools/anime_style.py ship_player  -> just those keys
+  python3 tools/anime_style.py --restore    -> put the originals back
+"""
+import os
+import shutil
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+SPRITES = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "sprites")
+ORIGINALS = os.path.join(ROOT, "external", "sprite_originals")
+PREFIXES = ("ship_", "station_", "npc_")
+
+OUTLINE = np.array([0.04, 0.05, 0.11])        # the ink: a deep navy
+LEVELS = 4                                     # cel tones
+CEL_MIX = 0.85                                 # how much of the flat tones (the rest: the original detail)
+SIMPLIFY = 0.6                                 # how much fine surface detail is smoothed away first
+SATURATION = 1.38
+RIM = 0.38                                     # the light rim's strength
+
+
+def _shift(a, dx, dy):
+    """a shifted by (dx, dy), zero-filled."""
+    out = np.zeros_like(a)
+    h, w = a.shape[:2]
+    xs, xd = (slice(0, w - dx), slice(dx, w)) if dx >= 0 else (slice(-dx, w), slice(0, w + dx))
+    ys, yd = (slice(0, h - dy), slice(dy, h)) if dy >= 0 else (slice(-dy, h), slice(0, h + dy))
+    out[yd, xd] = a[ys, xs]
+    return out
+
+
+def _dilate(mask, r):
+    out = mask.copy()
+    for dy in range(-r, r + 1):
+        for dx in range(-r, r + 1):
+            if dx * dx + dy * dy <= r * r + 0.5 and (dx or dy):
+                out |= _shift(mask, dx, dy)
+    return out
+
+
+def style(img: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
+    a = np.asarray(img.convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
+    rgb, alpha = a[..., :3], a[..., 3]
+    h, w = alpha.shape
+    solid = alpha > 0.5
+    # Flatter panels: smooth away fine surface noise (within the silhouette).
+    blur = rgb.copy()
+    for _ in range(2):
+        acc = np.zeros_like(blur)
+        for dy in (-1, 0, 1):
+            for dx in (-1, 0, 1):
+                acc += _shift(blur, dx, dy)
+        blur = acc / 9.0
+    rgb = np.where(solid[..., None], rgb * (1.0 - SIMPLIFY) + blur * SIMPLIFY, rgb)
+    # Cel shading: luminance snapped to a few flat tones, colour kept.
+    lum = rgb @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114], dtype=np.float32)
+    q = np.clip(np.round(lum * LEVELS) / LEVELS, 0.06, 1.0)
+    cel = np.clip(rgb * (q / np.maximum(lum, 0.02))[..., None], 0.0, 1.0)
+    rgb = rgb * (1.0 - CEL_MIX) + cel * CEL_MIX
+    # Livelier colours: more saturation, a touch more contrast.
+    grey = (rgb @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114], dtype=np.float32))[..., None]
+    rgb = np.clip(grey + (rgb - grey) * SATURATION, 0.0, 1.0)
+    rgb = np.clip((rgb - 0.5) * 1.08 + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)
+    # Line width in texture pixels: about 2.5 px at the size the sprite is shown.
+    k = max(2, int(round(max(w, h) / 75.0)))
+    # The rim: a bright band along the edges facing the light (top left).
+    lit_edge = solid & ~_shift(solid, k, k)
+    rgb = np.where(lit_edge[..., None], rgb + (1.0 - rgb) * RIM, rgb)
+    # Inner ink: a dark line just inside the silhouette.
+    inner = solid & ~(_shift(solid, 1, 0) & _shift(solid, -1, 0) & _shift(solid, 0, 1) & _shift(solid, 0, -1))
+    rgb = np.where(inner[..., None], rgb * 0.35 + OUTLINE * 0.65, rgb)
+    # The bold outline: the silhouette grown by k px, in ink, under the sprite.
+    grown = _dilate(solid, k)
+    ring = grown & ~solid
+    out = np.zeros((h, w, 4), dtype=np.float32)
+    out[..., :3] = np.where(ring[..., None], OUTLINE, rgb)
+    out[..., 3] = np.where(ring, 1.0, alpha)
+    # Keep soft edges where the sprite was half transparent over the ink.
+    soft = (alpha > 0.02) & ~solid
+    out[..., :3] = np.where(soft[..., None], rgb * alpha[..., None] + OUTLINE * (1 - alpha[..., None]), out[..., :3])
+    out[..., 3] = np.where(soft, 1.0, out[..., 3])
+    return Image.fromarray((out * 255.0 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA")
+
+
+def keys(args):
+    names = sorted(f[:-4] for f in os.listdir(SPRITES) if f.endswith(".png"))
+    if args:
+        return [n for n in names if n in args]
+    return [n for n in names if n.startswith(PREFIXES)]
+
+
+def main():
+    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
+    os.makedirs(ORIGINALS, exist_ok=True)
+    if "--restore" in sys.argv:
+        for f in os.listdir(ORIGINALS):
+            shutil.copy2(os.path.join(ORIGINALS, f), os.path.join(SPRITES, f))
+        print("restored", len(os.listdir(ORIGINALS)), "sprites")
+        return
+    n = 0
+    for key in keys(args):
+        src = os.path.join(ORIGINALS, key + ".png")
+        dst = os.path.join(SPRITES, key + ".png")
+        if not os.path.exists(src):
+            shutil.copy2(dst, src)
+        style(Image.open(src)).save(dst)
+        n += 1
+    print("styled", n, "sprites (originals in external/sprite_originals/)")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
